tagline: A governed AI coworker from Andrew Ng's GitHub, run on local Qwen models via Ollama

scenes.narration: Day 49: OpenWorker, an AI coworker published on Andrew Ng's GitHub, run on local Qwen models through Ollama.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: An agent that reads, writes and runs tools in your files
Every tool call is approval-gated by default
Every call is logged, approved or denied
scenes.narration: It works in your files. Every tool call needs approval by default, and every call is logged either way.

steps.narration: We ran the CLI headless and isolated from real settings, pointed at Ollama serving Qwen 2.5 at 7, 14 and 32 billion parameters.
When the model calls a tool like write_file, the approval gate decides. In ask mode with no terminal, the call is refused before it runs.
Approved or denied, every call lands in a SQLite audit log. Even with approvals bypassed, writes outside the workspace were blocked.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Runs out of 5 where 7B, 14B and 32B wrote a brief with all 7 facts from the meeting notes.
scenes.narration: On the README task, turning two meeting notes into a brief, 14B succeeded three times out of five and 7B once. The largest, 32B, never did: it searched for files named meeting, found none, and gave up.
All fifteen runs reported completed. The gate held; the outcome flag did not mean the job was done.
